title: People Ops Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook (2026) - v5001
author: Ava Patel
body:
Summary
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes and templates for hiring, candidate evaluation, employee onboarding, the performance & feedback cycle, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and engineering/product managers who run day-to-day people operations. Follow the procedures below to ensure consistent, compliant, and candidate-friendly experiences.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time and regular contractor hires across engineering, product, design, research, GTM, and corporate functions.
- Excludes executive-level hiring (VP+) and acquisitions, which use an extended approval path documented in /confluence/company-handbook/executive-hiring-process.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)
Objective: reduce time-to-fill while maintaining hiring quality and diversity. Target: median time-to-offer <= 45 days from requisition approval.

High-level steps:
1. Requisition & role definition
   - Hiring manager drafts a role brief in Lever and attaches: role purpose, top 3 outcomes for the first 6 months, required/desired competencies, salary band, and target diversity outreach plan.
   - People-ops reviews and posts to internal job board and external channels once approved.
2. Sourcing & screen
   - Sourcing owners run targeted outreach and update Lever weekly.
   - Initial recruiter screen (30 min) to confirm interest, base qualifications, remote/location constraints, and compensation expectations.
3. Interview loop & calibration
   - Standard loop (example for IC roles): recruiter screen -> technical/functional assessment -> paired coding/problem-solving (if applicable) -> system/design/architecture (senior roles) -> culture/leadership interview -> hiring manager debrief.
   - Panel composition: at least 2 interviewers from team/discipline and one cross-functional partner. Avoid candidate-facing panels with >4 interviewers.
   - Use the standard scorecard (attached template) and record notes in Lever. Interviewers must submit scores within 24 hours.
4. Offer & approvals
   - Hiring manager completes offer worksheet (salary band, equity, sign-on if applicable). People-ops performs market check and approval. Compensation approvals required for any deviation from band.
   - Send offer letter (JD + benefits summary + start logistics). Candidate should receive offer within 3 business days of final decision where possible.
5. Background check & close
   - Offers are contingent on successful background check and reference checks. People-ops initiates checks after offer acceptance and final ID verification.

Mandatory compliance & inclusivity checks:
- All job descriptions must include an EEO statement and clear accommodation language.
- Interview calibration: quarterly hiring calibration sessions per department led by people-ops to align scorecards and expectations.

2) Interviewer guidelines & scorecards
- Prepare: read candidate resume, list 3 focused questions tied to the role's top outcomes, and review the standard rubric.
- Use behavioral + technical questions; avoid hypotheticals unrelated to role.
- Assess on 4 axes: role fit, technical depth, communication & collaboration, and growth potential.
- Conflict-of-interest: disclose any personal relationships; recuse if required and document in Lever.

Scorecard (example fields) - store as template in /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples
- Candidate name (string)
- Interviewer (string)
- Role match (1-5)
- Technical competency (1-5)
- Communication (1-5)
- Collaboration & culture (1-5)
- Red flags (free text)
- Recommendation (hire/hold/no-hire)

3) New-hire onboarding (Day 0-90)
Goal: accelerate new hires to independent contribution in 30-90 days based on role level.

Pre-boarding (Day -7 to Day -1)
- People-ops checklist: send welcome email, confirm start date, share first-week agenda, benefits enrollment link, and new-hire handbook.
- IT & security: create account requests (Okta, GitHub, internal Slack, Google Workspace), request hardware, and set VPN & KMS access requests for private deployments if needed.

Day 0-7 (Orientation & team integration)
- Day 0: HR/People-ops orientation (benefits, compliance, payroll), manager 1:1 to review 30/60/90 plan, team lunch/intro.
- Technical access: confirm repo access, add to on-call rotations if applicable, and verify dev environment.

30/60/90 plan (template)
- 30 days: onboarding tasks completed, first small deliverable, basic infra access confirmed.
- 60 days: independently contribute to sprints, present a short project update to team.
- 90 days: full scope contribution, performance check-in with manager + people-ops.

Onboarding checklist (table)
| Area | Owner | Completion target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Offer acceptance & paperwork | People-ops | Day -7 to Day 0 |
| Laptop & hardware provisioned | IT | Day 0 |
| Okta, Google, Slack access | IT | Day 0 |
| Repo & infra access | Team lead | Day 2 |
| 30/60/90 plan created | Manager | Day 3 |
| First deliverable defined | Manager | Week 2 |

Documentation & training
- New hires must complete required security training and data handling modules within first 14 days. Product and infra readmes are available in /confluence/eng-platform.

4) Performance and feedback cycle
Cadence and objectives: Redwood runs an annual performance cycle with two formal calibration points (mid-year and year-end) and continuous feedback encouraged year-round.

Cycle timeline (example)
- Q1 start: goal-setting & expectations (manager + employee) — documented in Workday/HRIS.
- Mid-year (end of Q2): informal calibration & mid-year check-in. Managers submit mid-year flag list for calibration.
- Year-end (Q4): self-review, manager review, calibration, and compensation/bonus decisions.

Performance levels (standardized)
- Exceeds Expectations | Consistently delivers above scope and impacts cross-team outcomes.
- Meets Expectations | Fully meets role expectations and deliverables.
- Needs Improvement | Some gaps in delivery or collaboration; corrective plan required.
- Unsatisfactory | Fails to meet core responsibilities after sustained coaching.

Calibration & fairness
- Calibration panels include cross-functional managers, HRBP, and a people-ops representative.
- Calibration metrics: distribution targets by level, bias checks, and quota adjustments where needed.
- All compensation increases require an approved budget code and final sign-off by Head of People + Finance.

Continuous feedback expectations for managers
- Weekly 1:1s (30-60 minutes) with clear agenda items and action notes.
- Quarterly development check-ins and documented career conversations.
- Routine real-time feedback (praise & corrective) with suggested phrasing templates.

5) Performance improvement & separation process
- PIP (Performance Improvement Plan) steps:
  1. Document performance gaps and examples in a 1:1.
  2. Set a 30-90 day remediation plan with clear success criteria.
  3. Weekly manager check-ins and HRBP oversight.
  4. Final decision documented with HR and legal review.
- Separation checklist: exit interview, revoke access, final payroll & benefits reconciliation, equipment return. Use the checklist in /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks for security steps.

6) Manager playbook & responsibilities
Key manager responsibilities:
- Hiring: define role outcomes, partner with recruiter, and ensure inclusive interview panels.
- Onboarding: own the 30/60/90 plan and weekly check-ins during the first 90 days.
- Performance: set measurable goals, deliver timely feedback, and run calibration prep.
- Career growth: maintain a development plan and sponsor stretch opportunities.

Manager templates & scripts (examples)
- 1:1 agenda (shared Google Doc)
  - Quick wins (5 min), blockers (10 min), development (10 min), feedback (5 min), action items (5 min).
- Difficult feedback script
  - Fact: "On X date you..."
  - Impact: "The result was..."
  - Expectation: "Going forward we expect..."
  - Support: "I will help by..."
- Interview debrief template (required): candidate strengths, concerns, scorecard summary, recommended next step.

7) Metrics & reporting (people-ops dashboard)
Core metrics tracked weekly in People-ops dashboard:
- Time-to-fill (median days)
- Offer acceptance rate (%)
- New-hire retention at 90 days (%)
- Diversity of finalist pool (% underrepresented groups)
- Manager 1:1 frequency compliance (%)
Owners: People-ops owns reporting; Hiring managers must respond to data requests within 2 business days.

8) Escalation paths and ownership
- Compensation deviations: escalates to Head of People -> Finance.
- Legal/immigration issues: escalate directly to Legal & People-ops lead.
- Security access failures: engage Security oncall and IT immediately; use incident runbook.

Appendices
A. Offer letter checklist (required fields)
- Role title, start date, salary, equity (% or grant), benefits summary, probation period (if applicable), contingency clauses (background check), signing instructions.

B. Sample 30/60/90 plan (short form)
- 30 days: setup environment, complete onboarding modules, meet primary stakeholders.
- 60 days: deliver first feature, own a component.
- 90 days: lead a small project and present outcomes.

C. Quick templates (links)
- Interview scorecard template: /confluence/templates/interview-scorecard
- Offer worksheet: /confluence/templates/offer-worksheet
- 1:1 agenda: /confluence/templates/manager-1on1-agenda

Document ownership & updates
- Owner: People-ops (Ava Patel)
- Update cadence: review annually or after major policy changes.
- Feedback: send edits or requests to people-ops@redwoodai.com with "Playbook edit" subject.

This playbook should be used as the canonical source for people operations processes. When in doubt, contact your People-ops HRBP for role-specific guidance.
